chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a man asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about the earnings of the cupper, so he said to him, 'You have a cow.' He said, 'Yes.' He said to him, 'Feed it yourself and do not eat its milk.'

key_terms.اَلْحَجَّامِ: the cupper (one who performs cupping therapy)
key_terms.نَاضِحٌ: a cow (specifically one used for plowing or labor, often implying a source of milk)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the earnings of a cupper according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of a cow (*nadih*) to evaluate the earnings of a cupper, instructing the man to feed the cow but not consume its milk. Shia scholars interpret this as a nuanced ruling on the quality or purity of the income, suggesting that while the earnings are permissible, they may lack the full spiritual benefit or 'richness' associated with pure wealth, or that the cupper should maintain the means of production without fully exploiting its yield. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the ethical dimensions of trade and the distinction between mere permissibility (*halal*) and excellence (*mustahabb* or *afdal*) in one's livelihood.
